title: PhysWeep: Does a Video Generator Realize the Physics You Ask For?

paper.title: PhysWeep : Does a Video Generator Realize the Physics You Ask For?
paper.abstract:
Abstract Image-to-video generators are often credited with absorbing physical
dynamics as implicit world models, a claim the community currently checks
with plausibility scores that ask whether a clip looks consistent with
real-world motion. Plausibility is the wrong test on its own, because a
clip can look natural while encoding the wrong value of the governing
physical parameter, and no existing benchmark measures this gap directly. PhysWeep closes it with a fixed, label-free audit, treating a
frozen generator as a black box, recovering the realized parameter from
generated pixels, and reporting how often generation is trackable at all,
how far the realized value sits from the requested one, and which, if
either, of the literature’s two proposed failure mechanisms the data
support. A deterministic-simulator positive control confirms every score
is exactly checkable.
Applied to three open generators across six sweep axes, PhysWeep finds a specific, reproducible, previously undocumented failure.
Conditional on producing trackable motion, two of the three generate
confident, well-fit dynamics that converge to one of a small number of
fixed, wrong values selected by the sampling seed rather than by
the request, reproducing across two independent model families, two
physical systems, and an independent tracker. It matches neither the
prior reversion nor the case-based clamping the literature anticipates,
because the reversion target is seed-conditional rather than a single
global default, and a leave-one-out selection rule rejects both; the
in-range faithfulness slope is statistically indistinguishable from zero
wherever a response is estimable at all. A benchmark averaging over seeds
would never see this: each sample is confidently locked to a wrong
constant, exactly the failure a plausibility score is structurally blind
to. We release the protocol, suite, and analysis code as a reusable,
model-agnostic audit for generators that claim physics controllability.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Progress in video generation has revived an old hope: that a model trained only to predict pixels will, as a by-product, learn the laws that govern how the world moves [ 1 , 2 ] . The community has accordingly invested in measuring the physical plausibility of generated video, through benchmarks that ask human raters or VLM auto-raters whether motion looks right [ 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 , 8 ] . Plausibility is the wrong target on its own. A generator can produce a clip that is visually flawless yet encodes an incorrect value of the relevant parameter: a ball can fall along a smooth arc whose implied gravitational acceleration is simply wrong, and no plausibility rater will object, because the arc is locally consistent. The meaningful question is whether a generator realizes the specific physics implied by its conditioning, and whether that realization extends past the values the model saw most often in training. The second clause matters because a model that has internalized a law should treat the controlling parameter as a free variable, whereas one that has memorized typical motions falls back on what it has seen once pushed away from the common case. Recent roadmaps name this gap directly: surveys identify intrinsic faithfulness and controllability as the frontier and note that metrics for them remain scarce [ 9 , 10 ] , judge-based scores are hard to audit because a judge’s weights and APIs drift while a parameter recovered by a fixed estimator does not ( Sec. 2 ), and the gap is not incidental, since generators optimized for media prioritize visual smoothness over physical fidelity [ 11 ] . What is missing is a fixed, auditable measurement of whether a conditioned parameter is realized in the pixels. We turn “physical understanding” of a pretrained generator into a falsifiable measurement. Treat the frozen model as a black-box map from a conditioned parameter θ \theta to a trajectory, recover the realized θ ^ \hat{\theta} from generated pixels with no human labels, and quantify faithfulness, out-of-range behavior, and the form of any failure. PhysWeep also adjudicates between the two mechanisms the literature proposes: collapse to a single global default, or case-based mimicry of the nearest seen value. Our delta against the closest prior art ( Sec. 2 ) is a conjunction: a swept control parameter rather than a fixed default, on frozen black-box models, over six axes rather than gravity alone, with a continuous parameter-recovery readout rather than a binary or judge score. We do not claim to be first to recover physics from generated pixels. What is new is the determinant : the sampling seed is known to fix a generator’s appearance [ 12 ] , and we show it also fixes the physics, overriding an explicit request for it. KEY TAKEAWAY The sampling seed, not the request, picks the physics. A benchmark that averages over seeds reports a smooth mean and hides that each individual sample is confidently locked to a wrong constant.

sections.heading: Contributions
sections.text: 1. A reusable audit artifact. PhysWeep ships deterministic parameterized systems with ground-truth θ \theta , a fixed label-free estimator, and analysis code ( Sec. 5 ), validated by a simulator-video positive control. The estimator is fixed rather than learned, so the measurement is auditable by construction (unlike evolving VLM-judge scores [ 13 ] ), and it applies to any generator accepting one of our two conditioning channels, including ones claiming physics controllability. 2. Label-free metrics and a mechanism adjudication. A trackability rate, a Parameter Recovery Error ( PRE \mathrm{PRE} ) with its Extrapolation Gap ( EG \mathrm{EG} ) and a monotonicity score, two competing failure-form indices, Prior-Reversion ( PRI \mathrm{PRI} ) and Case-Based ( CBI \mathrm{CBI} ), and a leave-one-out rule that lets the data choose between global-default collapse and nearest-value mimicry, or reject both ( Sec. 4 ) — together turning “did the generator learn physics” into a falsifiable, pre-registered test rather than a qualitative impression. 3. A formal account of the failure we find, and the statistic that identifies it. We define seed-conditional defaults and prove they force PRI → 1 \mathrm{PRI}\to 1 with a vanishing held-out R 2 R^{2} (so rejecting both prior hypotheses is a derived prediction, not an unexplained negative), and that the same signature arises from noise, so PRI \mathrm{PRI} alone cannot establish the mechanism, and give a Seed Determination Index that can ( Sec. 4.1 ). This closes a real gap in how the field reports results: an experiment that is not seed-resolved cannot tell seed-locking apart from a well-behaved generator with noisy output, and we show that distinction is exactly what is at stake here. sections.heading: 2 Related work
sections.text: A large family of benchmarks scores whether generated video looks physical: human and learned raters of physical commonsense [ 3 , 4 ] , broader law taxonomies [ 5 , 8 ] , real footage [ 6 ] , conservation-law metrics [ 7 ] , first-principles organization [ 14 ] , likelihood on valid-versus-invalid pairs [ 15 ] , and Physics and Controllability scored by VLM proxies [ 16 , 17 ] . These ask whether a clip looks right, not whether it realizes a requested parameter. Lin et al. [13] argue such judges are hard to reproduce because they evolve, and an evaluation on real systems reports a fine-tuned judge scoring clean recordings only moderately [ 18 ] ; our plausibility contrast is an independent instance on synthetic stimuli. Closer to our own readout, Li et al. [19] measure falling dynamics in generated video to drive physics post-training, and Thozhiyoor et al. [20] recover an effective gravity from pixels, show that current generators under-accelerate toward a fixed sub-Earth value, and eliminate metric-scale and frame-rate confounds with a unit-free two-object timing test; Le et al. [21] use a similar readout as a verifiable post-training reward. This is the closest prior art and we do not claim priority over it, but all three fix the target law to gravity and characterize a model’s default behavior, whereas our question is orthogonal and complementary: given a parameter the user asks for , across six sweep axes, does the realized value move with the request. Their fixed- θ \theta result and our swept- θ \theta result answer different halves of the same worry. A separate line establishes that the initial noise fixed by the sampling seed leaves a strong, recoverable imprint on what a diffusion model produces [ 12 ] , but for generated appearance ; Definition 2 extends this to dynamics , and to our knowledge the seed has not previously been shown to fix a quantitative physical parameter. A further wave of 2025–2026 methods claims physics controllability through editable simulation, latent dynamics, geometry guidance, force-vector or explicit-parameter conditioning, and inference-time extrapolation [ 22 , 23 , 24 , 25 , 26 , 27 , 28 , 29 ] ; PhysWeep asks what a frozen model does beforehand and supplies the fixed measurement against which such claims can be re-checked without training access. Appendix F extends this section with the mechanism literature [ 30 , 31 ] , adjacent property-readout and VLM-based work [ 32 , 33 , 34 , 35 , 36 ] , and classic prediction/planning benchmarks [ 37 , 38 , 39 , 40 ] .

sections.text: Figure 2 sketches the loop described here. For each grid value θ i \theta_{i} and seed z j z_{j} we render conditioning frames, generate a continuation, track the observable and fit f f in closed form to obtain ( θ ^ i ​ j , R i ​ j 2 ) (\hat{\theta}_{ij},R^{2}_{ij}) ; clips with R i ​ j 2 < 0.8 R^{2}_{ij}<0.8 are marked non-physical and excluded from PRE \mathrm{PRE} , and that rate is reported alongside every result. A VLM rater scores the same clips. Rendering uses a small deterministic 2D engine with no external assets; tracking is color-blob centroiding, with CoTracker3 [ 41 ] as an independent second tracker in ablation. Pseudocode is in Appendix A . The pipeline is inference-only, run on a shared NVIDIA A100-SXM4 (40 GB), not a single consumer GPU (CogVideoX’s 25.3 25.3 GB peak, with tiling, exceeds a 24 GB budget), for an estimated ∼ 57 \sim\!57 total GPU-hours across all runs; the estimate’s derivation and per-model figures are in Appendix D .

sections.heading: How θ \theta is conditioned
sections.text: Models accept different inputs, so we treat the channel as a controlled axis. Frame-implied conditioning supplies rendered frames whose motion already implies θ \theta and asks the model to continue, isolating dynamics from semantics. Text-specified conditioning supplies a first frame plus a prompt naming the regime, for example on the Moon versus on Jupiter, testing whether a named control moves the realized parameter. Section 6 reports which channel each result uses, since only one model admits both.

sections.heading: Protocol
sections.text: We tested three frozen open generators, each within reach of a single high-end GPU (VRAM figures in Appendix D ): LTX-Video [ 42 ] , CogVideoX-5B-I2V [ 43 ] , DynamiCrafter 512 [ 44 ] . Stable Video Diffusion [ 45 ] was dropped before any run because its pipeline accepts no text prompt; a quantized Wan [ 46 ] was considered and not run. Plausibility is contrasted against, not used as, the main metric via one VLM auto-rater [ 47 ] ; no human subset and no VBench-2.0 score were collected . Before running we pre-committed which of four outcomes would confirm or refute each hypothesis, whatever the sweep actually showed: (1) faithful in-range, fails out-of-range, prior reversion or case clamping selected — the field’s own anticipated headline; (2) no conditioning effect ( β ≈ 0 \beta\approx 0 ); (3) faithful even out-of-range ( EG ≈ 0 \mathrm{EG}\approx 0 ), a surprising positive result reported as such; or (4) neither hypothesis fits. Whichever occurred would drive the abstract, title, and contributions; Sec. 6 names which two of the four the sweep produced. We use m ≥ 5 m\geq 5 seeds per ( θ i , model ) (\theta_{i},\text{model}) , report 95 % 95\% bootstrap CIs and effect sizes rather than p p -values alone, test PRE ⁡ ( S out ) > PRE ⁡ ( S in ) \mathrm{PRE}(S_{\text{out}})>\mathrm{PRE}(S_{\text{in}}) by paired bootstrap, and report held-out R 2 R^{2} and Δ \Delta AIC for selection. Model repositories and licenses are in Appendix D , which also discloses that no explicit commit/revision was pinned when loading any model, so each resolved to that repository’s default-branch head at run time; Appendix E is the reproducibility checklist.

sections.heading: The failure is seed-locked, not untrackable noise
sections.text: The three models reach the same null slope through visibly different behavior, confirmed by frame inspection. LTX-Video mostly fails to generate any real fall: the conditioned disk stays near its initial position regardless of the requested g g or how the prompt describes it, tested up to “extremely strong gravity, like Jupiter, violent rapid acceleration downward.” CogVideoX and DynamiCrafter instead generate confident, well-tracked motion that is simply the wrong amount, with recovered g ^ \hat{g} clustering tightly by sampling seed and close to independent of the request: on CogVideoX one seed gives g ^ ≈ − 11.4 ± 0.03 \hat{g}\approx-11.4\pm 0.03 across every in-range g ∈ { 5 , 7 , 9.8 , 12 , 15 } g\in\{5,7,9.8,12,15\} and another gives − 7.1 ± 0.2 -7.1\pm 0.2 ( Fig. 1 ), reproducing out-of-range on the same seeds. That second mode also rules out the reading that the trackability rate invites, that these models simply cannot render minimalist synthetic scenes and the survivors are flukes: if the stimulus were merely un-renderable, the recovered values clearing the gate would be scattered, not tight. They are not (within-seed dispersion 0.03 0.03 – 0.13 0.13 , individual-clip fit R 2 R^{2} up to 1.000 1.000 , clusters reappearing under an independent tracker). Confident, well-fit, seed-locked motion is what a model ignoring θ \theta produces, not what one failing to render produces, so we state the headline conditionally: conditional on producing physically trackable motion, none of the three models detectably honors a text-specified physical parameter. Trackability bounds the coverage of that claim, not its validity.

sections.heading: The signature crosses architectures and physical systems
sections.text: The pattern is not specific to the projectile. LTX-Video’s near-total-inertia failure generalizes, with four of its five remaining axes below 6 % 6\% trackable. CogVideoX’s seed-determined convergence generalizes only where clips survive the gate, which fails entirely on spring-mass and inclined slide; on bouncing-ball, every gated seed converges to a recovered restitution in [ 0.97 , 1.00 ] [0.97,1.00] regardless of the request, and DynamiCrafter independently reproduces the identical signature on the same system ( e ^ = 0.99 \hat{e}=0.99 – 1.00 1.00 across the full grid, individual-clip R 2 = 1.000 R^{2}=1.000 ): two architectures landing on the same wrong-but-confident behavior. Three of DynamiCrafter’s axes ( ω \omega , ζ \zeta , spring-mass) are separately bounded by its fixed 16 16 -frame output, too short for one oscillation period, a capability ceiling we keep distinct from a conditioning failure throughout.

sections.heading: A third variant: a split, not a single, default
sections.text: DynamiCrafter’s inclined slide adds a variant the two-hypothesis framework does not name. One seed behaves like the single-default cases above, at μ ^ ≈ 1.80 \hat{\mu}\approx 1.80 across the whole grid; a second shows two tight clusters, μ ^ ≈ 4.7 \hat{\mu}\approx 4.7 ( std = 0.04 \mathrm{std}=0.04 ) in-range and ≈ 7.6 \approx 7.6 ( std = 0.13 \mathrm{std}=0.13 ) out-of-range. That is neither ignoring θ \theta nor a single global default. We name it the split-default pattern.

By Proposition 3 that is exactly what a seed-conditional default predicts. Checked against what it should track, the correlation between tracker fit R 2 R^{2} and P P is 0.075 0.075 , 0.019 0.019 and − 0.164 -0.164 respectively, indistinguishable from zero: a CogVideoX clip whose trajectory collapses into texture noise ( R 2 = 0.48 R^{2}=0.48 ) scored 5 / 5 5/5 while a cleanly tracked LTX-Video fall ( R 2 = 0.99 R^{2}=0.99 ) scored 1 / 5 1/5 (truncation, parsing failure and file corruption ruled out). This rater does not track physical coherence here, which is why we report trackability as a separate metric.

sections.heading: The result survives every nuisance parameter we varied
sections.text: (a) Tracker swap. CoTracker3 [ 41 ] rerun on every clip agrees strongly where both trackers clear the gate (LTX-Video projectile r = 0.984 r=0.984 , inclined slide r = 0.997 r=0.997 ); DynamiCrafter agreement is strong on the reported seed cluster but disagrees in sign on a second seed, so the phenomenon replicates under an independent tracker while one cluster’s value is tracker-sensitive. (b) Nuisance parameters. Across five disk-size and frame-rate rescalings, four guidance values, two prompt templates and two conditioning resolutions, the in-range slope stays small and unstable in sign (LTX-Video − 0.26 -0.26 to + 1.38 +1.38 over 13 variants; DynamiCrafter − 0.25 -0.25 to + 0.12 +0.12 over 7, since neither guidance nor resolution applies to it); CogVideoX’s columns are uninformative rather than confirmatory, since no clip clears the gate at this sweep’s shorter frame budget. (c) Gate sensitivity. The null does not flip at any threshold from 0.5 0.5 to 0.95 0.95 .

sections.heading: Changing the conditioning channel does not rescue it
sections.text: We ran frame-implied conditioning on DynamiCrafter, the one model with a reachable official multi-frame checkpoint, on the three axes where its text-channel data is usable (projectile conditioned on first and middle frame, since its true last frame is degenerate by construction and the middle frame’s height is confirmed to vary with g g ). It does not recover faithfulness: every gated projectile clip converges to g ^ ≈ 0 \hat{g}\approx 0 (slope 0.017 0.017 , CI [ − 0.008 , 0.047 ] [-0.008,0.047] ), so where the text channel gave seed-diverse defaults, the frame channel collapses to one near-universal default of no fall, not a degenerate-conditioning artifact. Inclined slide is starker still, μ ^ \hat{\mu} near 1.7 1.7 – 1.8 1.8 while true μ \mu runs from 0.01 0.01 to 1.00 1.00 . Dropped rates (pooled, from a separate, larger-seed-count run than Table 2 ) are lower under the frame channel on all three axes ( 10 % 10\% vs. 30 % 30\% projectile, 23 % 23\% vs. 29 % 29\% inclined slide, 63 % 63\% vs. 86 % 86\% bouncing ball), so the two channels are not directly comparable cell-for-cell against Table 2 , but neither one is faithful.

sections.heading: 7 Limitations
sections.text: Trackability bounds coverage. Trackability never exceeds 80 % 80\% and is 0 % 0\% on ten of eighteen pairs. Section 6 argues from the survivors’ seed-locked tightness that this is not simply un-renderable output, which is why the headline is conditional, but what these models do where nothing clears the gate remains open: a contemporaneous study recovering gravity from current generators on photorealistic stimuli obtained usable trajectories where we largely do not [ 20 ] . Model currency. The gap is specific rather than generic: we test LTX-Video and CogVideoX-5B while later releases in both families exist, and omit the open models most often credited with physically coherent motion. It also looks closable, since Wan reports an 8.19 8.19 GB text-to-video variant at 1.3 1.3 B [ 46 ] plausibly inside our budget, though not the image-to-video checkpoint we would need. Design gaps, closed and remaining. The pipeline has a positive control (simulator-video recovery at β = 1.0001 \beta=1.0001 ) and now a negative one: permuting θ \theta labels within each model-axis pair and refitting β \beta , 10,000 10{,}000 times on the five slope-estimable pairs, places every observed β \beta well inside its own null distribution (two-sided permutation p p from 0.56 0.56 to 0.91 0.91 ), calibrating “indistinguishable from zero” against an actual null. A TOST against a pre-specified smallest effect ϵ = 0.2 \epsilon=0.2 at α = 0.05 \alpha=0.05 (SE backed out from each pair’s bootstrap CI) shows only LTX-Video/projectile is formally equivalent to zero ( p TOST < 0.001 p_{\text{TOST}}<0.001 ); the other four, including the two inclined-slide pairs whose CIs also contain β = 1 \beta=1 , do not clear the bar ( p TOST p_{\text{TOST}} from 0.14 0.14 to 0.64 0.64 ), consistent with underpowered estimates rather than a plausible large effect. So “no detectable response” is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence, at four of these five pairs; only LTX-Video/projectile is positively established. Native clip length is still confounded with model identity ( 24 24 , 49 49 trimmed to 24 24 , 16 16 frames), so cross-model trackability comparisons are not clean. Channel, coverage, ceilings. All results but the channel ablation use text conditioning; frame-implied conditioning is untested for LTX-Video and CogVideoX for the pipeline reasons above. Adjudication covers 8 of 18 pairs, DynamiCrafter’s 16-frame output makes three axes untestable for reasons unrelated to conditioning, and a joint ( ω , ζ ) (\omega,\zeta) pendulum sweep returned 0 % 0\% trackability (best R 2 = 0.14 R^{2}=0.14 ), which we report as uninformative rather than negative. Plausibility contrast and realism. One rater on one prompt does not track physical coherence here, and we tested no other prompt, larger VLM or human raters. The suite also trades ecological validity for identifiability, so conclusions concern controllable low-dimensional dynamics.

sections.heading: 8 Conclusion
sections.text: We reframe learning physics from video, for a generator, as a falsifiable label-free question of parameter faithfulness, and supply a black-box diagnostic, three metrics with a stated identifiability condition, a controllable suite, and a protocol separating plausibility from correctness. Applied to three frozen open generators it finds that, conditional on producing trackable motion, none detectably honors a text-specified parameter, and that the failure is not merely absent signal: two of three converge to a few fixed, wrong values selected by the sampling seed rather than the request, reproducibly across model families, axes and trackers. The seed is already known to fix a generator’s appearance [ 12 ] ; here it fixes the physics. A benchmark averaging over seeds reports a smooth mean and hides that each sample is locked to a wrong constant, so seed-resolved reporting is not optional. The next targets are whether the signature survives on photorealistic stimuli and on current generators. REPRODUCIBILITY All systems are procedurally generated by a seeded deterministic engine, models are public, trackers and fitting are off-the-shelf or closed-form, and no labels are used; the analysis code and system generators are released as anonymized supplementary material. Every generation is keyed to an explicit integer seed, with m ≥ 5 m\geq 5 seeds per grid point recorded per clip. The full checklist is Appendix E ; grids, seed counts, model repositories, licences and compute are in Appendix D . DATA AND CODE AVAILABILITY The analysis code and system generators are available at https://github.com/KurbanIntelligenceLab/physweep ; All models used are public and frozen; repositories and licences are listed in Appendix D . COMPETING INTERESTS No human-subjects data was collected and the diagnostic is meant to prevent overclaiming about video generators as physical simulators, which has safety relevance in robotics and science. Per WACV’s LLM policy: an assistant drafted the initial consistency proof ( Appendix B ), the physics-recovery fitters and prose throughout. Both were verified by the authors before use, the proof by hand against its three stated assumptions (trackability, identifiability, regularity; Appendix B ), which surfaced the ω \omega -versus- ω d \omega_{d} correction and one latent code bug, and every fitter against closed-form trajectories with a passing smoke test. A careful line-by-line check of both supplementary proofs ( Proposition 3 and the appendix’s consistency and misspecification proofs, Appendix B and Appendix C ) was performed during finalization, independently re-deriving the crossed-design independence argument, the OLS-slope and population- R 2 R^{2} convergence steps, the SDI formula against the standard ICC(1) estimator, and the Definition 2 nesting claim, with no error found. The assistant did not choose hypotheses, design grids or interpret results, and the authors take responsibility for all content.

sections.text: The released smoke test records a limitation of CBI \mathrm{CBI} as defined. If an out-of-range grid lies entirely on one side of the in-range band, the clamp prediction min ⁡ ( θ , θ edge ) \min(\theta,\theta_{\text{edge}}) is constant across S out S_{\text{out}} and is therefore indistinguishable from the null mean model, so CBI ≈ 0 \mathrm{CBI}\approx 0 and clamping cannot be adjudicated at any sample size. sections.heading: Appendix E Reproducibility checklist
sections.text: WACV’s author guide points to the Reproducibility Checklist as a guide rather than a mandated form, and encourages voluntary code submission. We record the substantive items here. Code. Metrics, bootstrap CIs, mechanism selection, and the synthetic smoke test ( physweep_metrics.py ), the system generators ( physweep/render.py ), the tracker ( physweep/track.py , both blob-centroid and the CoTracker3 wrapper), and every experiment driver script ( experiments/*.py , one per experiment plus the consolidated plausibility-and-robustness harness) exist in the project repository. Data. Fully procedural, no external assets, no human annotation, seeded and deterministic. Models. All public, all frozen, inference only. No training or fine-tuning was performed at any point. Randomness. Every generation is keyed to an explicit integer seed; m ≥ 5 m\geq 5 seeds per grid point; seeds are recorded per clip. Statistics. All intervals are 95 % 95\% paired bootstraps over ( θ i , seed ) (\theta_{i},\text{seed}) ; effect sizes are reported alongside p p -values; multiplicity across the six paired-bootstrap extrapolation tests is handled by a Holm correction. Raw outputs. Per-clip records (model, system, seed, θ \theta , θ ^ \hat{\theta} , fit R 2 R^{2} , in/out-of-range split, and, for the plausibility pass, the VLM score) exist as JSON files in the project’s results/ directory, one file per model-system pair plus the plausibility-scored variants — every number in this paper and its supplementary tables was recomputed directly from these files during finalization, not carried forward from memory.

sections.heading: Appendix F Extended related work
sections.text: This section extends Sec. 2 with material not central enough to the paper’s own contribution to justify main-text space, but relevant to situating it.

sections.heading: Mechanism and memorization
sections.text: Kang et al. [30] find in-distribution success with out-of-distribution case-based behavior (the source of the case-clamping hypothesis we test), and the memorization literature links such collapse to overestimated training modes amplified by classifier-free guidance [ 31 ] ; we turn these into a testable dichotomy ( Sec. 3 ) and a guidance-scale ablation ( Sec. 6 ).

sections.heading: Adjacent but distinct measurement approaches
sections.text: Property-readout work recovers physical quantities from input videos via internal features [ 32 ] or probes diffusion states [ 33 ] , characterizing the encoder where we measure generation without weights or activations. VLMs are separately used to plan plausible generation [ 34 ] and judge implausibility [ 35 ] , and recent analyses question whether they reason about physical transformations at all [ 36 ] — consistent with our own finding ( Sec. 6 ) that a VLM plausibility rater does not track physical coherence on our stimuli. Classic benchmarks [ 37 , 38 ] evaluate prediction or planning rather than generation, and quality metrics [ 39 , 40 ] are orthogonal to all of the above: they score visual fidelity, not parameter faithfulness.

Abstract Image-to-video generators are often credited with absorbing physical dynamics as implicit world models, a claim the community currently checks with plausibility scores that ask whether a clip looks consistent with real-world motion. Plausibility is the wrong test on its own, because a clip can look natural while encoding the wrong value of the governing physical parameter, and no existing benchmark measures this gap directly. PhysWeep closes it with a fixed, label-free audit, treating a frozen generator as a black box, recovering the realized parameter from generated pixels, and reporting how often generation is trackable at all, how far the realized value sits from the requested one, and which, if either, of the literature’s two proposed failure mechanisms the data support. A deterministic-simulator positive control confirms every score is exactly checkable. Applied to three open generators across six sweep axes, PhysWeep finds a specific, reproducible, previously undocumented failure. Conditional on producing trackable motion, two of the three generate confident, well-fit dynamics that converge to one of a small number of fixed, wrong values selected by the sampling seed rather than by the request, reproducing across two independent model families, two physical systems, and an independent tracker. It matches neither the prior reversion nor the case-based clamping the literature anticipates, because the reversion target is seed-conditional rather than a single global default, and a leave-one-out selection rule rejects both; the in-range faithfulness slope is statistically indistinguishable from zero wherever a response is estimable at all. A benchmark averaging over seeds would never see this: each sample is confidently locked to a wrong constant, exactly the failure a plausibility score is structurally blind to. We release the protocol, suite, and analysis code as a reusable, model-agnostic audit for generators that claim physics controllability. 1 Introduction Progress in video generation has revived an old hope: that a model trained only to predict pixels will, as a by-product, learn the laws that govern how the world moves [ 1 , 2 ] . The community has accordingly invested in measuring the physical plausibility of generated video, through benchmarks that ask human raters or VLM auto-raters whether motion looks right [ 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 , 8 ] . Plausibility is the wrong target on its own. A generator can produce a clip that is visually flawless yet encodes an incorrect value of the relevant parameter: a ball can fall along a smooth arc whose implied gravitational acceleration is simply wrong, and no plausibility rater will object, because the arc is locally consistent. The meaningful question is whether a generator realizes the specific physics implied by its conditioning, and whether that realization extends past the values the model saw most often in training. The second clause matters because a model that has internalized a law should treat the controlling parameter as a free variable, whereas one that has memorized typical motions falls back on what it has seen once pushed away from the common case. Recent roadmaps name this gap directly: surveys identify intrinsic faithfulness and controllability as the frontier and note that metrics for them remain scarce [ 9 , 10 ] , judge-based scores are hard to audit because a judge’s weights and APIs drift while a parameter recovered by a fixed estimator does not ( Sec. 2 ), and the gap is not incidental, since generators optimized for media prioritize visual smoothness over physical fidelity [ 11 ] . What is missing is a fixed, auditable measurement of whether a conditioned parameter is realized in the pixels. We turn “physical understanding” of a pretrained generator into a falsifiable measurement. Treat the frozen model as a black-box map from a conditioned parameter θ \theta to a trajectory, recover the realized θ ^ \hat{\theta} from generated pixels with no human labels, and quantify faithfulness, out-of-range behavior, and the form of any failure. PhysWeep also adjudicates between the two mechanisms the literature proposes: collapse to a single global default, or case-based mimicry of the nearest seen value. Our delta against the closest prior art ( Sec. 2 ) is a conjunction: a swept control parameter rather than a fixed default, on frozen black-box models, over six axes rather than gravity alone, with a continuous parameter-recovery readout rather than a binary or judge score. We do not claim to be first to recover physics from generated pixels. What is new is the determinant : the sampling seed is known to fix a generator’s appearance [ 12 ] , and we show it also fixes the physics, overriding an explicit request for it. KEY TAKEAWAY The sampling seed, not the request, picks the physics. A benchmark that averages over seeds reports a smooth mean and hides that each individual sample is confidently locked to a wrong constant. Contributions 1. A reusable audit artifact. PhysWeep ships deterministic parameterized systems with ground-truth θ \theta , a fixed label-free estimator, and analysis code ( Sec. 5 ), validated by a simulator-video positive control. The estimator is fixed rather than learned, so the measurement is auditable by construction (unlike evolving VLM-judge scores [ 13 ] ), and it applies to any generator accepting one of our two conditioning channels, including ones claiming physics controllability. 2. Label-free metrics and a mechanism adjudication. How θ \theta is conditioned Models accept different inputs, so we treat the channel as a controlled axis. Frame-implied conditioning supplies rendered frames whose motion already implies θ \theta and asks the model to continue, isolating dynamics from semantics. Text-specified conditioning supplies a first frame plus a prompt naming the regime, for example on the Moon versus on Jupiter, testing whether a named control moves the realized parameter. Protocol We tested three frozen open generators, each within reach of a single high-end GPU (VRAM figures in Appendix D ): LTX-Video [ 42 ] , CogVideoX-5B-I2V [ 43 ] , DynamiCrafter 512 [ 44 ] . Stable Video Diffusion [ 45 ] was dropped before any run because its pipeline accepts no text prompt; a quantized Wan [ 46 ] was considered and not run. Plausibility is contrasted against, not used as, the main metric via one VLM auto-rater [ 47 ] ; no human subset and no VBench-2.0 score were collected .
